extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of coke manufacturing facilities (coke oven batteries and PQBS), industry stakeholders, and regulatory compliance personnel
extracted.subtask_description: Final rule rescinding an interim final rule and reinstating compliance deadlines and standards under the NESHAP for coke oven batteries and pushing/quenching/battery stacks (PQBS), including pollutant-specific MACT standards, fenceline monitoring, reporting, and operation/maintenance requirements. The document identifies applicability, statutory authority, affected CFR sections, and statutory/EO determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability — Which entities this action applies to
rubrics_metrics.description: The Coke Oven Batteries (COB) source category includes emissions from the batteries themselves. The Pushing, Quenching, and Battery Stacks (PQBS) source category includes emissions from pushing and quenching operations, and from battery stacks at a coke oven facility. A coke oven facility is defined as a facility engaged in the manufacturing of metallurgical coke by the destructive distillation of coal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides NAICS codes: COB (40 CFR part 63, subpart L) = 324199 ('All Other Petroleum and Coal Products Manufacturing'), PQBS (40 CFR part 63, subpart CCCCC) = 331110 ('Iron and Steel Mills and Ferroalloy Manufacturing'). The section is a guide for readers regarding the entities likely affected; consult the person in FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT for specific applicability questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority — Clean Air Act section 112
rubrics_metrics.description: The Clean Air Act (CAA), and CAA section 112 in particular (42 U.S.C. 7412), provides the statutory authority to issue this action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies the legal basis for the rulemaking and frames the EPA's authority to promulgate and rescind regulatory provisions under the NESHAP program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescission of IFR; reinstatement of 2024 compliance deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA is rescinding the interim final rule (IFR) that extended certain compliance deadlines and effectively reinstituting the compliance deadlines set forth in the 2024 final rule revising the Coke Ovens NESHAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a result of the rescission, the original deadlines in the 2024 rule revisions apply to the source categories; EPA concluded public comment did not show immediate compliance difficulties that justified the IFR extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PQBS MACT standards — pushing operations pollutants
rubrics_metrics.description: New emission standards based on MACT for pushing operations: acid gases (AG), hydrogen cyanide (HCN), mercury (Hg), and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAH) (which is also a surrogate for dioxins and furans (D/F), formaldehyde, and volatile organic HAP (VOHAP)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These pollutant categories are the basis for MACT-based emission standards for pushing operations; PAH is used as a surrogate for several other HAPs per the rule text.

rubrics_metrics.name: PQBS MACT standards — battery stacks pollutants
rubrics_metrics.description: New emission standards based on MACT for battery stacks: acid gases (AG), hydrogen cyanide (HCN), mercury (Hg), and particulate matter (PM) (as a surrogate for non-Hg HAP metals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PM is treated as a surrogate for non-mercury hazardous air pollutant metals in battery stack standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: PQBS MACT standards — HNR HRSG main stacks pollutants
rubrics_metrics.description: New emission standards based on MACT for HNR heat recovery steam generator (HRSG) main stacks: acid gases (AG), mercury (Hg), PAH (which is also a surrogate for formaldehyde), and PM (as a surrogate for non-Hg HAP metals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies the pollutant list applicable to HRSG main stacks and surrogate relationships used for regulatory compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: PQBS MACT standards — HNR bypass/waste heat (B/W) stacks pollutants
rubrics_metrics.description: New emission standards based on MACT for HNR bypass/waste heat (B/W) stacks: acid gases (AG), formaldehyde (which is also a surrogate for VOHAP), mercury (Hg), PAH, and PM (as a surrogate for non-Hg HAP metals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies pollutant categories for bypass/waste heat stacks and notes surrogate assignments (formaldehyde for VOHAP, PM for non-Hg HAP metals).

rubrics_metrics.name: PQBS work practice MACT standard for battery stacks (PAH, D/F, VOHAP)
rubrics_metrics.description: A new MACT standard, in the form of a good combustion practices work practice standard, for PAH, D/F, and VOHAP emitted from battery stacks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This standard is a work practice (good combustion practices) rather than a numeric emission limit for the listed pollutants emitted from battery stacks.

rubrics_metrics.name: COB requirements — fenceline monitoring, leak standards, and pressure monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: For the COB source category, the rescinded IFR had extended compliance deadlines for fenceline monitoring requirements; revised leak standards for doors, lids, and offtakes; and revised pressure monitoring requirements for oven doors at heat and nonrecovery (HNR) facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With the IFR rescinded, the original 2024 rule compliance dates and requirements for these COB provisions apply; the rule also amends specific CFR sections (e.g., §63.314 fenceline monitoring provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fenceline monitoring provisions (§63.314)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each by-product coke oven battery facility as defined in §63.301, beginning no later than July 7, 2025, the owner or operator of a coke manufacturing facility shall conduct sampling along the facility property boundary and analyze the samples in accordance with paragraphs (a) through (g) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies when fenceline monitoring must begin and that sampling/analysis must follow the detailed procedures set out in the referenced paragraphs (a)-(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for by-product coke oven batteries (§63.302)
rubrics_metrics.description: On and after July 7, 2025: emission limitations and requirements applied to each coke oven battery utilizing a new recovery technology shall be less than the following emission limitations or shall result in an overall annual emissions rate for coke oven emissions for the battery that is lower than that obtained by the following emission limitations on and after July 7, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the benchmark emission limitations for by-product batteries and allows alternative demonstration by showing a lower overall annual emissions rate; applies beginning July 7, 2025.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for nonrecovery coke oven batteries (§63.303)
rubrics_metrics.description: The date for compliance with paragraphs (a)(1)(i) and (ii) of this section is on and after July 7, 2025. For certain provisions the date for compliance is on and after July 7, 2025, or upon initial startup, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies compliance timing for nonrecovery batteries, including startup exceptions where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for compliance date extension (§63.304)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to §63.304 revise provisions governing standards for compliance date extension; paragraph (b)(8) is revised to read 'On and after July 7, 2025:' followed by the applicable provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates how compliance date extension provisions are structured and the dates from which they operate; detailed conditions for extensions remain in the referenced paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance dates for Subpart CCCCC (§63.7283)
rubrics_metrics.description: (d)(1) If you have an existing affected source or a new or reconstructed affected source for which construction or reconstruction commenced on or before August 16, 2023, you must be in compliance no later than January 5, 2026. (d)(2) If you have a new or reconstructed affected source for which construction or reconstruction commenced after August 16, 2023, you must be in compliance no later than January 5, 2026, or upon startup, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides specific compliance deadlines tied to construction/reconstruction dates and clarifies the 'upon startup' exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operation and maintenance requirements — site-specific good combustion practices (§63.7300)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning January 5, 2026, you must identify and implement a set of site-specific good combustion practices for each battery. These good combustion practices should correspond to your standard operating procedures for maintaining the proper and efficient combustion within battery waste heat flues. Good combustion practices include, but are not limited to, the elements listed in paragraphs (c)(4)(i) through (v) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires documented, site-specific SOP-aligned combustion practices; the rule enumerates example elements (c)(4)(i)-(v) which should be implemented as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and recordkeeping — electronic reporting via CEDRI (§63.311 and §63.7341)
rubrics_metrics.description: §63.311(h): Beginning on July 7, 2025, or once the report template for this subpart has been available on the EPA's Compliance and Emissions Data Reporting Interface (CEDRI) website for one year, whichever date is later, submit all subsequent reports to the EPA via the CEDRI according to §63.9(k) except that confidential business information (CBI) should be submitted according to paragraph (k) of this section. §63.7341(f): Beginning on July 7, 2026, or once the report template for this subpart has been available on the CEDRI website for one year, whichever date is later, submit all subsequent reports to the EPA via the CEDRI according to §63.9(k) except that CBI should be submitted according to paragraph (h) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies electronic submission requirements, the triggering dates (or one-year availability of templates), compliance with §63.9(k), and special handling of CBI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docket availability and protection of confidential business information
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA has established dockets for this action under Docket ID Nos. EPA-HQ-OAR-2002-0085 and EPA-HQ-OAR-2003-0051. All documents in the docket are listed on https://www.regulations.gov/. Although listed, some information is not publicly available, e.g., Confidential Business Information (CBI) or other information whose disclosure is restricted by statute. Certain other material, such as copyrighted material, is not placed on the internet and will be publicly available only in hard copy form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how regulated parties and other stakeholders can access supporting documents, the handling of CBI, and the availability of hard copy materials at the EPA Docket Center/Public Reading Room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and Executive Order determinations (Regulatory analyses and applicability)
rubrics_metrics.description: The action is not a significant regulatory action under Executive Order 12866; it does not impose new information collection burden under the PRA; the EPA certifies no significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities under the RFA; the action does not contain an unfunded mandate of $100 million or more under UMRA; it does not have federalism or tribal implications; EO13045 and EO13211 do not apply; NTTAA does not apply; the action is subject to the Congressional Review Act (CRA) and is not a major action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarizes the EPA's determinations under multiple statutes and Executive Orders, which affect analytical and procedural requirements for the rulemaking and signal the agency's findings about economic and intergovernmental impacts.
